item.title: India to grow 7% in FY27, El Nino impact to drive food prices higher: S&P
item.description: S&P Global Ratings on Monday said it expects India's GDP to grow 7 per cent in both the current and subsequent fiscal years with the country poised to be one of the fastest-growing economies in the Asia Pacific region in 2027. S&P said food prices are likely to rise in APAC economies, especially India, because of El Nino, and it anticipates a further 25 basis points policy rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India in December. S&P's Economic Outlook for Asia-Pacific said high energy prices will remain the largest macro headwind and the global AI build-out the largest tailwind for the region, but both forces should ease a bit in 2027. "We expect Vietnam and India to be the region's fastest-growing economies in 2027," S&P said. The rating agency said it expects India's GDP growth to be 7 per cent in the current as well as next fiscal year. item.title: Wider access to finance, digital economy key to eradicate poverty: FM
item.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday said wider access to finance, markets and the digital economy would be key to eradicating poverty and ensuring those lifted out of it do not slip back. Quoting the World Bank report which showed that nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, Sitharaman said the Narendra Modi government has focused on targeted interventions, measurable outcomes and tailored schemes to remove deprivations. "Garibi is not merely a shortage of income or wages. A household without a secure roof, safe water, sanitation or healthcare remains vulnerable even when its income rises. One illness can wipe out savings and push a family back into poverty," the minister said in a LinkedIn post titled 'The Decade India Turned the Tide on Poverty'. She said welfare schemes like Jal Jeevan Mission, Ayushman Bharat, PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, and Swachh Bharat are together acting as "insurance against the shocks" that once pushed families

item.title: West Bengal govt in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres in Singur: CM
item.description: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday said his government was in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres of land in Singur in Hooghly district, a day after Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar announced Ashok Leyland would set up a truck manufacturing plant there. Singur was the site of Tata Motors' Nano small-car factory, for which the then Left Front government acquired around 997 acres in 2006. The acquisition triggered a prolonged farmers' agitation led by Mamata Banerjee, following which Tata Motors moved the project to Sanand in Gujarat in 2008. In August 2016, the Supreme Court quashed the land acquisition and ordered that the land be returned to the farmers. "The West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) had been tasked with acquiring the 997 acres, and negotiations with farmers were underway to purchase the land at a reasonable rate," Adhikari told reporters. He said the government would "do something" with the land, without mentioning Ashok Leyland

item.title: Oil, gas import bill up 60% in Oct as Brent surges, LPG use declines
item.description: India's net oil and gas import bill rose 60 per cent year-on-year to USD 16 billion in October as Brent crude averaged USD 124.77 a barrel, almost double that of a year earlier, according to data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), part of the oil ministry. The net bill was USD 10.0 billion in October 2025. Crude imports alone cost USD 19.5 billion, against USD 10.4 billion a year ago, even though volumes rose only 11 per cent to 23.3 million tonnes. LNG imports cost USD 1.3 billion, and petroleum product exports brought in USD 6.3 billion. Brent averaged USD 116.77 in September and USD 64.75 in October 2025. The Indian basket averaged USD 119.91 in October, against USD 65.08 a year earlier. Over April-October, the net import bill reached USD 97.7 billion, up from USD 70.3 billion a year earlier. Crude imports rose 2.7 per cent in volume but cost USD 111.0 billion, against USD 72.3 billion. Consumption of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) fell 12.3 per cent in October
item.bs:keywords: India oil import bill, India gas import bill, crude oil imports, Brent crude prices, PPAC data, LPG consumption, LPG imports, Strait of Hormuz, LNG imports, petroleum product exports, India's oil import dependence, diesel consumption, petrol consumption, oil prices

item.title: India, Canada conclude sixth round of talks for proposed trade pact
item.description: India and Canada have concluded the sixth round of negotiations for a trade agreement, aimed at unlocking new opportunities in trade and investment, and diversifying supply chains, an official statement said on Saturday. The negotiations covered key areas, including trade in goods, trade in services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property and investment promotion, the commerce ministry said. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal held a meeting with Glenn Purves, Vice Minister of International Trade of Canada, and his delegation to review the progress of negotiations for the proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). The ten-day talks concluded on November 20. "Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to concluding an ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful agreement that delivers tangible benefits to farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both countries," it said.
item.bs:keywords: India-Canada trade agreement, India-Canada CEPA negotiations, India Canada trade talks, Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, India-Canada trade and investment

item.title: India's core sector growth hit 31-month high of 10.9% in October
item.description: Output of key infrastructure industries rose 10.9 per cent in October 2026, up from 0.8 per cent in the year-ago month, driven by strong performance in coal, iron ore, electricity and cement. According to the official data released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry on Friday, the core sector expanded by 8.2 per cent in September 2026. Among segments, iron ore output rose by 26.4 per cent, electricity by 21.6 per cent, coal by 23.1 per cent, and cement by 15.4 per cent. During April-October this fiscal, these nine segments expanded by 6 per cent against 2.3 per cent in the same period last year.
